CONCEPT_SYSTEM_DESIGN.name: System Design
CONCEPT_SYSTEM_DESIGN.definition: The process of defining the architecture, components, modules, interfaces, and data for a system to satisfy specified requirements.

CONCEPT_DISTRIBUTED_SYSTEMS.name: Distributed Systems
CONCEPT_DISTRIBUTED_SYSTEMS.definition: A system whose components are located on different networked computers, which communicate and coordinate their actions by passing messages to one another.

CONCEPT_STORAGE.name: Storage
CONCEPT_STORAGE.definition: The process and mechanisms for retaining digital data for later retrieval and use.

CONCEPT_SECURITY.name: Security
CONCEPT_SECURITY.definition: The protection of information systems from theft or damage to the hardware, software, and to the information on them, as well as from disruption or misdirection of the services they provide.

CONCEPT_ASYNCHRONOUS_SYSTEMS.name: Asynchronous Systems
CONCEPT_ASYNCHRONOUS_SYSTEMS.definition: Systems where operations can proceed independently without waiting for each other to complete, often using messaging to coordinate.

CONCEPT_INTERNET_WORKS.name: How the Internet works
CONCEPT_INTERNET_WORKS.definition: How a request physically travels from your laptop to a server, involving IP addressing, routers, and packets.

CONCEPT_IP_ADDRESSING.name: IP Addressing
CONCEPT_IP_ADDRESSING.definition: A numerical label assigned to each device connected to a computer network that uses the Internet Protocol for communication.

CONCEPT_ROUTERS.name: Routers
CONCEPT_ROUTERS.definition: Networking devices that forward data packets between computer networks.

CONCEPT_PACKETS.name: Packets
CONCEPT_PACKETS.definition: Units of data that are routed between an origin and a destination on the internet or any other packet-switched network.

CONCEPT_OSI_MODEL.name: OSI Model
CONCEPT_OSI_MODEL.definition: A conceptual framework that standardizes the functions of a telecommunication or computing system into seven abstraction layers.

CONCEPT_TCP_IP_STACK.name: TCP/IP Stack
CONCEPT_TCP_IP_STACK.definition: A four-layer conceptual model used to describe network communication protocols in real systems, practically based on the OSI model.

CONCEPT_TCP.name: TCP
CONCEPT_TCP.definition: Transmission Control Protocol, providing reliable ordered delivery of data between applications.

CONCEPT_UDP.name: UDP
CONCEPT_UDP.definition: User Datagram Protocol, providing fast connectionless delivery of data with no guarantees of reliability or order.

CONCEPT_DNS_RESOLUTION.name: DNS Resolution
CONCEPT_DNS_RESOLUTION.definition: The process of translating a human-readable domain name into an IP address.

CONCEPT_HTTP.name: HTTP
CONCEPT_HTTP.definition: Hypertext Transfer Protocol, governing the request/response cycle for web communication.

CONCEPT_HTTPS.name: HTTPS
CONCEPT_HTTPS.definition: Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure, an extension of HTTP that adds a secure layer via TLS handshake for encrypted communication.

CONCEPT_CLIENT_SERVER_ARCHITECTURE.name: Client-Server Architecture
CONCEPT_CLIENT_SERVER_ARCHITECTURE.definition: A computing model where clients (requesters of services) send requests to servers (providers of services).

CONCEPT_PROCESSES.name: Processes
CONCEPT_PROCESSES.definition: An instance of a computer program that is being executed by one or many threads.

CONCEPT_THREADS.name: Threads
CONCEPT_THREADS.definition: The smallest sequence of programmed instructions that can be managed independently by a scheduler, often within a process.

CONCEPT_CONCURRENCY.name: Concurrency
CONCEPT_CONCURRENCY.definition: The ability of different parts of a program or system to be executed out-of-order or in partial order, potentially overlapping in execution time.

CONCEPT_PARALLELISM.name: Parallelism
CONCEPT_PARALLELISM.definition: The ability of a system to perform multiple computations or processes simultaneously, often using multiple CPU cores.

CONCEPT_OS_MEMORY_BASICS.name: OS Memory Basics
CONCEPT_OS_MEMORY_BASICS.definition: Fundamental concepts of how an operating system manages and allocates memory to processes and threads.

CONCEPT_SCALABILITY.name: Scalability
CONCEPT_SCALABILITY.definition: The ability of a system to handle a growing amount of work or its potential to be enlarged to accommodate that growth.

CONCEPT_VERTICAL_SCALING.name: Vertical Scaling
CONCEPT_VERTICAL_SCALING.definition: Scaling up by increasing the resources (CPU, RAM) of a single machine.

CONCEPT_HORIZONTAL_SCALING.name: Horizontal Scaling
CONCEPT_HORIZONTAL_SCALING.definition: Scaling out by adding more machines to a system.

CONCEPT_LATENCY.name: Latency
CONCEPT_LATENCY.definition: The time delay between a cause and effect, typically the time per request.

CONCEPT_THROUGHPUT.name: Throughput
CONCEPT_THROUGHPUT.definition: The rate at which work is processed, typically requests per second.

CONCEPT_BANDWIDTH.name: Bandwidth
CONCEPT_BANDWIDTH.definition: The maximum data transfer rate of a network or internet connection, typically max data per second.

CONCEPT_AVAILABILITY.name: Availability
CONCEPT_AVAILABILITY.definition: The proportion of time a system is functional and accessible, often measured in 'nines' (e.g., 99.9%).

CONCEPT_RELIABILITY.name: Reliability
CONCEPT_RELIABILITY.definition: The probability that a system will operate correctly for a specified period under specified conditions, often involving redundancy and failover.

CONCEPT_FAULT_TOLERANCE.name: Fault Tolerance
CONCEPT_FAULT_TOLERANCE.definition: The ability of a system to continue operating without interruption when one or more of its components fail, often through redundancy and graceful degradation.

CONCEPT_CAP_THEOREM.name: CAP Theorem
CONCEPT_CAP_THEOREM.definition: A fundamental theorem stating that a distributed system cannot simultaneously guarantee Consistency, Availability, and Partition tolerance; it must sacrifice one.

CONCEPT_PACELC_THEOREM.name: PACELC Theorem
CONCEPT_PACELC_THEOREM.definition: An extension of the CAP theorem, stating that in the presence of network partitions (P), a system must choose between Availability (A) and Consistency (C), else (E) when there is no partition, it must choose between Latency (L) and Consistency (C).

CONCEPT_CONSISTENCY_MODELS.name: Consistency Models
CONCEPT_CONSISTENCY_MODELS.definition: Different guarantees about how data updates are propagated and seen by different nodes in a distributed system, including strong, eventual, causal, and read-your-writes consistency.

CONCEPT_REST.name: REST
CONCEPT_REST.definition: Representational State Transfer, an architectural style for networked applications that defines a set of constraints for creating web services, typically using a request/response API over HTTP.

CONCEPT_GRAPHQL.name: GraphQL
CONCEPT_GRAPHQL.definition: A query language for APIs and a runtime for fulfilling those queries with your existing data, offering flexible querying and efficient data fetching.

CONCEPT_GRPC.name: gRPC
CONCEPT_GRPC.definition: A high-performance Remote Procedure Call (RPC) framework that can run in any environment, enabling client and server applications to communicate transparently.

CONCEPT_WEBSOCKETS.name: WebSockets
CONCEPT_WEBSOCKETS.definition: A communication protocol that provides full-duplex communication channels over a single TCP connection, enabling real-time interactions between a client and server.

CONCEPT_LOAD_BALANCERS.name: Load Balancers
CONCEPT_LOAD_BALANCERS.definition: Devices or software that distribute incoming network traffic across multiple servers to improve responsiveness and availability.

CONCEPT_L4_LOAD_BALANCING.name: L4 Load Balancing
CONCEPT_L4_LOAD_BALANCING.definition: Load balancing at the transport layer (Layer 4 of the OSI model), based on IP addresses and ports.

CONCEPT_L7_LOAD_BALANCING.name: L7 Load Balancing
CONCEPT_L7_LOAD_BALANCING.definition: Load balancing at the application layer (Layer 7 of the OSI model), based on content, URL, HTTP headers, etc.

CONCEPT_LOAD_BALANCING_ALGORITHMS.name: Load Balancing Algorithms
CONCEPT_LOAD_BALANCING_ALGORITHMS.definition: Methods used by load balancers to distribute traffic, such as round robin, least connections, IP hash, and weighted algorithms.

CONCEPT_API_GATEWAYS.name: API Gateways
CONCEPT_API_GATEWAYS.definition: A single entry point for all clients, handling requests by routing them to appropriate microservices, performing authentication, rate limiting, and request aggregation.

CONCEPT_REVERSE_PROXIES.name: Reverse Proxies
CONCEPT_REVERSE_PROXIES.definition: A server that retrieves resources on behalf of a client from one or more servers, providing an additional layer of abstraction or control to ensure security, high availability, and performance.

CONCEPT_CDNS.name: CDNs (Content Delivery Networks)
CONCEPT_CDNS.definition: Networks of geographically distributed servers that cache content at edge locations closer to users to reduce latency and improve content delivery speed.

CONCEPT_DNS_GEO_ROUTING.name: DNS-based Geo-routing
CONCEPT_DNS_GEO_ROUTING.definition: Using DNS to route user requests to the closest or best-performing server based on geographical location, often in conjunction with CDNs.

CONCEPT_SQL_DATABASES.name: SQL Databases
CONCEPT_SQL_DATABASES.definition: Relational databases that store data in tables with predefined schemas, using SQL (Structured Query Language) for querying.

CONCEPT_NOSQL_DATABASES.name: NoSQL Databases
CONCEPT_NOSQL_DATABASES.definition: Non-relational databases that provide flexible schemas and are designed for specific data models and use cases, offering high scalability and availability.

CONCEPT_INDEXING.name: Indexing
CONCEPT_INDEXING.definition: A technique used to optimize the speed of data retrieval in a database by creating a data structure, like B-Trees or hash indexes, that quickly locates records.

CONCEPT_B_TREES.name: B-Trees
CONCEPT_B_TREES.definition: A self-balancing tree data structure that maintains sorted data and allows searches, sequential access, insertions, and deletions in logarithmic time, commonly used for database indexes.

CONCEPT_HASH_INDEXES.name: Hash Indexes
CONCEPT_HASH_INDEXES.definition: An index that uses a hash function to map keys to a location in storage, suitable for exact match lookups.

CONCEPT_COMPOSITE_INDEXES.name: Composite Indexes
CONCEPT_COMPOSITE_INDEXES.definition: An index on multiple columns of a table, used to optimize queries that involve those columns together.

CONCEPT_NORMALIZATION.name: Normalization
CONCEPT_NORMALIZATION.definition: The process of organizing columns and tables of a relational database to minimize data redundancy and improve data integrity.

CONCEPT_DENORMALIZATION.name: Denormalization
CONCEPT_DENORMALIZATION.definition: The process of adding redundant data to a database, often by combining tables, to improve read performance at the expense of increased data redundancy.

CONCEPT_DATABASE_REPLICATION.name: Database Replication
CONCEPT_DATABASE_REPLICATION.definition: The process of copying data from one database server (leader) to other servers (followers) to ensure high availability and improve read scalability.

CONCEPT_LEADER_FOLLOWER_REPLICATION.name: Leader-Follower Replication
CONCEPT_LEADER_FOLLOWER_REPLICATION.definition: A replication model where one node (leader) processes all writes, and other nodes (followers) replicate the leader's data and handle read requests.

CONCEPT_MULTI_LEADER_REPLICATION.name: Multi-Leader Replication
CONCEPT_MULTI_LEADER_REPLICATION.definition: A replication model where multiple nodes can accept writes, with conflicts resolved asynchronously, often used for geographically distributed systems.

CONCEPT_LEADERLESS_REPLICATION.name: Leaderless Replication
CONCEPT_LEADERLESS_REPLICATION.definition: A replication model where any node can accept writes, and data consistency is maintained through mechanisms like quorum reads/writes.

CONCEPT_SYNCHRONOUS_REPLICATION.name: Synchronous Replication
CONCEPT_SYNCHRONOUS_REPLICATION.definition: Replication where a write operation is not considered complete until all replicas have confirmed receipt of the data, ensuring strong consistency.

CONCEPT_ASYNCHRONOUS_REPLICATION.name: Asynchronous Replication
CONCEPT_ASYNCHRONOUS_REPLICATION.definition: Replication where a write operation is considered complete once the leader has written the data, with replicas updating eventually, prioritizing performance over strong consistency.

CONCEPT_SHARDING.name: Sharding
CONCEPT_SHARDING.definition: The process of horizontally partitioning a database into smaller, more manageable pieces called shards, distributing data across multiple machines.

CONCEPT_PARTITIONING.name: Partitioning
CONCEPT_PARTITIONING.definition: Dividing a database into independent sections, which can be done horizontally (sharding) or vertically (by columns).

CONCEPT_HOT_SHARD_PROBLEM.name: Hot-Shard Problem
CONCEPT_HOT_SHARD_PROBLEM.definition: A situation in sharded databases where one shard receives a disproportionately large amount of traffic, becoming a bottleneck.

CONCEPT_ACID_PROPERTIES.name: ACID Properties
CONCEPT_ACID_PROPERTIES.definition: A set of properties (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability) guaranteeing that database transactions are processed reliably, typically found in relational databases.

CONCEPT_BASE_PROPERTIES.name: BASE Properties
CONCEPT_BASE_PROPERTIES.definition: A set of properties (Basically Available, Soft State, Eventually Consistent) that characterize the trade-offs in NoSQL databases, prioritizing availability and partition tolerance over immediate consistency.

CONCEPT_KEY_VALUE_DATABASES.name: Key-Value Databases
CONCEPT_KEY_VALUE_DATABASES.definition: A type of NoSQL database that stores data as a collection of key-value pairs, where each key is unique and maps to a value.

CONCEPT_DOCUMENT_DATABASES.name: Document Databases
CONCEPT_DOCUMENT_DATABASES.definition: A type of NoSQL database that stores data in flexible, semi-structured document formats (like JSON or XML), often without a predefined schema.

CONCEPT_COLUMN_FAMILY_DATABASES.name: Column-Family Databases
CONCEPT_COLUMN_FAMILY_DATABASES.definition: A type of NoSQL database that stores data in column families, which are groups of related columns, optimizing for sparse data and high write throughput.

CONCEPT_GRAPH_DATABASES.name: Graph Databases
CONCEPT_GRAPH_DATABASES.definition: A type of NoSQL database that uses graph structures for semantic queries with nodes, edges, and properties to store and represent data.

CONCEPT_CACHING.name: Caching
CONCEPT_CACHING.definition: Storing copies of frequently accessed data in a temporary, faster storage location to reduce latency and improve performance.

CONCEPT_CACHING_HIERARCHY.name: Caching Hierarchy
CONCEPT_CACHING_HIERARCHY.definition: The tiered system of different cache types (client, CDN, application, database) used to optimize data retrieval closest to the user.

CONCEPT_CLIENT_CACHE.name: Client Cache
CONCEPT_CLIENT_CACHE.definition: Cache stored on the user's device (e.g., browser cache) to speed up subsequent requests.

CONCEPT_APPLICATION_CACHE.name: Application Cache
CONCEPT_APPLICATION_CACHE.definition: Cache stored within the application layer, often in memory, to speed up data access for that specific application.

CONCEPT_DATABASE_CACHE.name: Database Cache
CONCEPT_DATABASE_CACHE.definition: Cache integrated with or directly fronting a database to store query results or frequently accessed data from the database.

CONCEPT_CACHE_STRATEGIES.name: Cache Strategies
CONCEPT_CACHE_STRATEGIES.definition: Different patterns for interacting with a cache and a primary data store, including cache-aside, write-through, write-back, and read-through.

CONCEPT_CACHE_ASIDE.name: Cache-aside
CONCEPT_CACHE_ASIDE.definition: A caching strategy where the application explicitly checks the cache first, and if data is not found, fetches it from the database and populates the cache.

CONCEPT_WRITE_THROUGH.name: Write-through
CONCEPT_WRITE_THROUGH.definition: A caching strategy where data is written simultaneously to the cache and the primary data store, ensuring data consistency.

CONCEPT_WRITE_BACK.name: Write-back
CONCEPT_WRITE_BACK.definition: A caching strategy where data is written to the cache first and then asynchronously written to the primary data store, offering faster write performance.

CONCEPT_READ_THROUGH.name: Read-through
CONCEPT_READ_THROUGH.definition: A caching strategy where the cache itself is responsible for fetching data from the underlying data store if it's not present, abstracting the data source from the application.

CONCEPT_CACHE_EVICTION_POLICIES.name: Cache Eviction Policies
CONCEPT_CACHE_EVICTION_POLICIES.definition: Algorithms that determine which items to remove from a cache when it reaches its capacity, such as LRU, LFU, and FIFO.

CONCEPT_LRU.name: LRU (Least Recently Used)
CONCEPT_LRU.definition: An eviction policy that discards the least recently used items first from the cache.

CONCEPT_LFU.name: LFU (Least Frequently Used)
CONCEPT_LFU.definition: An eviction policy that discards the items that have been used the fewest times from the cache.

CONCEPT_FIFO_CACHE_EVICTION.name: FIFO (First-In, First-Out) Cache Eviction
CONCEPT_FIFO_CACHE_EVICTION.definition: An eviction policy that discards the oldest items in the cache first.

CONCEPT_REDIS.name: Redis
CONCEPT_REDIS.definition: An open-source, in-memory data structure store, used as a database, cache, and message broker, supporting various data structures.

CONCEPT_MEMCACHED.name: Memcached
CONCEPT_MEMCACHED.definition: A free and open-source, high-performance, distributed memory object caching system, primarily used for speeding up dynamic web applications by alleviating database load.

CONCEPT_MESSAGE_QUEUES.name: Message Queues
CONCEPT_MESSAGE_QUEUES.definition: A form of asynchronous communication where messages are placed onto a queue and processed by a consumer at a later time, providing point-to-point delivery.

CONCEPT_PUB_SUB.name: Pub/Sub (Publish-Subscribe)
CONCEPT_PUB_SUB.definition: A messaging pattern where senders (publishers) do not program messages to be sent directly to specific receivers (subscribers), but instead categorize published messages into topics or channels for fan-out delivery.

CONCEPT_APACHE_KAFKA.name: Apache Kafka
CONCEPT_APACHE_KAFKA.definition: A distributed streaming platform that allows publishing, subscribing to, storing, and processing streams of records, characterized by topics, partitions, consumer groups, and offsets.

CONCEPT_KAFKA_TOPICS.name: Kafka Topics
CONCEPT_KAFKA_TOPICS.definition: Categories or feed names to which records are published in Kafka.

CONCEPT_KAFKA_PARTITIONS.name: Kafka Partitions
CONCEPT_KAFKA_PARTITIONS.definition: Divisions of a Kafka topic, allowing for parallel processing and scalability.

CONCEPT_KAFKA_CONSUMER_GROUPS.name: Kafka Consumer Groups
CONCEPT_KAFKA_CONSUMER_GROUPS.definition: A set of consumers that jointly consume data from a set of topics in Kafka, with each partition being consumed by only one consumer within the group.

CONCEPT_KAFKA_OFFSETS.name: Kafka Offsets
CONCEPT_KAFKA_OFFSETS.definition: A sequential ID number given to each record within a Kafka partition, representing its position.

CONCEPT_EVENT_DRIVEN_ARCHITECTURE.name: Event-Driven Architecture
CONCEPT_EVENT_DRIVEN_ARCHITECTURE.definition: An architectural style where decoupled services communicate by producing and consuming events, often involving event sourcing.

CONCEPT_EVENT_SOURCING.name: Event Sourcing
CONCEPT_EVENT_SOURCING.definition: An architectural pattern where all changes to application state are stored as a sequence of immutable events.

CONCEPT_RATE_LIMITING.name: Rate Limiting
CONCEPT_RATE_LIMITING.definition: A technique to control the number of requests a client can make to a server within a given time window, protecting systems from overload or abuse.

CONCEPT_TOKEN_BUCKET.name: Token Bucket Algorithm
CONCEPT_TOKEN_BUCKET.definition: A rate limiting algorithm where tokens are added to a bucket at a fixed rate, and each request consumes a token; requests are processed only if tokens are available.

CONCEPT_LEAKY_BUCKET.name: Leaky Bucket Algorithm
CONCEPT_LEAKY_BUCKET.definition: A rate limiting algorithm where requests are added to a bucket and processed at a constant rate, smoothing out bursts of traffic.

CONCEPT_FIXED_WINDOW_RATE_LIMITING.name: Fixed Window Rate Limiting
CONCEPT_FIXED_WINDOW_RATE_LIMITING.definition: A rate limiting algorithm that counts requests within a fixed time window, resetting the count at the start of each new window.

CONCEPT_SLIDING_WINDOW_RATE_LIMITING.name: Sliding Window Rate Limiting
CONCEPT_SLIDING_WINDOW_RATE_LIMITING.definition: A rate limiting algorithm that offers a more accurate rate limit by taking into account a moving average of requests over a rolling time window.

CONCEPT_CONSISTENT_HASHING.name: Consistent Hashing
CONCEPT_CONSISTENT_HASHING.definition: A hashing technique that minimizes data movement when nodes are added or removed from a distributed system, ensuring efficient distribution of keys across nodes.

CONCEPT_DATABASE_SCALING_PATTERNS.name: Database Scaling Patterns
CONCEPT_DATABASE_SCALING_PATTERNS.definition: Strategies for improving the performance and capacity of databases, including read replicas, connection pooling, and CQRS.

CONCEPT_READ_REPLICAS.name: Read Replicas
CONCEPT_READ_REPLICAS.definition: Copies of a primary database that serve read-only queries, offloading read traffic from the master database to improve performance and scalability.

CONCEPT_CONNECTION_POOLING.name: Connection Pooling
CONCEPT_CONNECTION_POOLING.definition: A technique used to manage and reuse database connections, reducing the overhead of establishing new connections for each request.

CONCEPT_CQRS.name: CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation)
CONCEPT_CQRS.definition: An architectural pattern that separates the read and update operations for a data store, often leading to different models for each.

CONCEPT_BLOOM_FILTERS.name: Bloom Filters
CONCEPT_BLOOM_FILTERS.definition: A space-efficient probabilistic data structure used to test whether an element is a member of a set, with a possibility of false positives but no false negatives.

CONCEPT_HEARTBEATS.name: Heartbeats
CONCEPT_HEARTBEATS.definition: Periodic signals sent from one system component to another to indicate that it is still operational and responsive.

CONCEPT_HEALTH_CHECKS.name: Health Checks
CONCEPT_HEALTH_CHECKS.definition: Automated checks to verify the operational status and responsiveness of a system or service.

CONCEPT_CONSENSUS_ALGORITHMS.name: Consensus Algorithms
CONCEPT_CONSENSUS_ALGORITHMS.definition: Protocols that allow multiple distributed processes to agree on a single data value or state, even in the presence of failures.

CONCEPT_PAXOS.name: Paxos
CONCEPT_PAXOS.definition: A family of protocols for solving consensus in a network of unreliable processors, among the most influential but complex consensus algorithms.

CONCEPT_RAFT.name: Raft
CONCEPT_RAFT.definition: A consensus algorithm designed to be understandable and provide a robust fault-tolerant distributed system, typically simpler than Paxos.

CONCEPT_DISTRIBUTED_TRANSACTIONS.name: Distributed Transactions
CONCEPT_DISTRIBUTED_TRANSACTIONS.definition: Transactions that involve multiple independent computational units or resources, requiring all or none of the operations to commit across all participants to maintain atomicity.

CONCEPT_TWO_PHASE_COMMIT.name: Two-Phase Commit (2PC)
CONCEPT_TWO_PHASE_COMMIT.definition: A distributed algorithm that ensures all nodes in a distributed transaction either commit or abort the transaction, aiming for atomicity across services.

CONCEPT_SAGA_PATTERN.name: Saga Pattern
CONCEPT_SAGA_PATTERN.definition: A pattern that manages distributed transactions as a sequence of local transactions, where each local transaction updates data and publishes an event that triggers the next local transaction, with compensating transactions for failures.

CONCEPT_VECTOR_CLOCKS.name: Vector Clocks
CONCEPT_VECTOR_CLOCKS.definition: A system for generating a partial ordering of events in a distributed system, used to determine causal relationships without a global clock.

CONCEPT_QUORUMS.name: Quorums
CONCEPT_QUORUMS.definition: A mechanism in distributed systems to ensure data consistency and availability by requiring a minimum number of nodes to agree (read quorum R, write quorum W) before an operation is considered successful, often R+W > N (total nodes).

CONCEPT_IDEMPOTENCY.name: Idempotency
CONCEPT_IDEMPOTENCY.definition: The property of an operation that it can be applied multiple times without changing the result beyond the initial application, making retried requests safe in distributed systems.

CONCEPT_MONOLITH_ARCHITECTURE.name: Monolith Architecture
CONCEPT_MONOLITH_ARCHITECTURE.definition: A software architecture where an application is built as a single, unified unit, encompassing all its functionalities in one codebase.

CONCEPT_MICROSERVICES_ARCHITECTURE.name: Microservices Architecture
CONCEPT_MICROSERVICES_ARCHITECTURE.definition: An architectural style that structures an application as a collection of loosely coupled services, each developed, deployed, and managed independently.

CONCEPT_MODULAR_MONOLITH.name: Modular Monolith
CONCEPT_MODULAR_MONOLITH.definition: An architectural approach that structures a monolithic application internally into distinct modules with clear boundaries, aiming to gain some benefits of microservices while retaining the simplicity of a single deployment unit.

CONCEPT_SERVICE_DISCOVERY.name: Service Discovery
CONCEPT_SERVICE_DISCOVERY.definition: The process by which applications and services locate each other on a network, especially in dynamic, distributed environments.

CONCEPT_CLIENT_SIDE_SERVICE_DISCOVERY.name: Client-Side Service Discovery
CONCEPT_CLIENT_SIDE_SERVICE_DISCOVERY.definition: A service discovery pattern where the client (or an intermediary) queries a service registry to find available service instances and then directly calls them.

CONCEPT_SERVER_SIDE_SERVICE_DISCOVERY.name: Server-Side Service Discovery
CONCEPT_SERVER_SIDE_SERVICE_DISCOVERY.definition: A service discovery pattern where a load balancer or router queries a service registry and routes requests to available service instances without the client being aware of the discovery process.

CONCEPT_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_PATTERN.name: Circuit Breaker Pattern
CONCEPT_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_PATTERN.definition: A design pattern used to prevent a network or service failure from cascading to other services, by 'tripping' calls to a failing dependency after a certain threshold.

CONCEPT_BULKHEAD_PATTERN.name: Bulkhead Pattern
CONCEPT_BULKHEAD_PATTERN.definition: A design pattern used to isolate elements of a system into pools so that if one fails, the others can continue to function, preventing cascading failures.

CONCEPT_BACKEND_FOR_FRONTEND.name: Backend-for-Frontend (BFF)
CONCEPT_BACKEND_FOR_FRONTEND.definition: An architectural pattern where a separate backend service is created for each frontend application (e.g., web, mobile), allowing tailored APIs for specific client needs.

CONCEPT_AUTHENTICATION.name: Authentication
CONCEPT_AUTHENTICATION.definition: The process of verifying the identity of a user, system, or process, typically by checking credentials like username/password or tokens.

CONCEPT_AUTHORIZATION.name: Authorization
CONCEPT_AUTHORIZATION.definition: The process of determining what a verified user, system, or process is permitted to do or access within a system.

CONCEPT_OAUTH_2_0.name: OAuth 2.0
CONCEPT_OAUTH_2_0.definition: An open standard for access delegation, commonly used as a way for Internet users to grant websites or applications access to their information on other websites without giving them the passwords.

CONCEPT_JWT.name: JWT (JSON Web Tokens)
CONCEPT_JWT.definition: A compact, URL-safe means of representing claims to be transferred between two parties, often used for authentication and authorization.

CONCEPT_ENCRYPTION.name: Encryption
CONCEPT_ENCRYPTION.definition: The process of encoding information in such a way that only authorized parties can access it, including symmetric (same key for encrypt/decrypt) and asymmetric (different keys) methods.

CONCEPT_TLS.name: TLS (Transport Layer Security)
CONCEPT_TLS.definition: A cryptographic protocol designed to provide communication security over a computer network, widely used for HTTPS.

CONCEPT_DDOS_PROTECTION.name: DDoS Protection
CONCEPT_DDOS_PROTECTION.definition: Measures taken to mitigate or prevent Distributed Denial of Service attacks, which aim to make a service unavailable by overwhelming it with traffic.

CONCEPT_INPUT_VALIDATION.name: Input Validation
CONCEPT_INPUT_VALIDATION.definition: The process of ensuring that user input conforms to expected formats, types, and constraints to prevent security vulnerabilities and data corruption.

CONCEPT_LOGGING.name: Logging
CONCEPT_LOGGING.definition: The process of recording events and data about the execution of a system or application, typically for debugging, monitoring, and auditing purposes.

CONCEPT_METRICS.name: Metrics
CONCEPT_METRICS.definition: Quantifiable measures used to track the performance and health of a system, such as CPU usage, memory, request rates, or error counts.

CONCEPT_TRACING.name: Tracing
CONCEPT_TRACING.definition: The process of tracking the full lifecycle of a request as it propagates through a distributed system, providing visibility into inter-service communication and performance.

CONCEPT_MONITORING.name: Monitoring
CONCEPT_MONITORING.definition: The continuous process of collecting, analyzing, and displaying data about the performance, health, and usage of a system.

CONCEPT_ALERTING.name: Alerting
CONCEPT_ALERTING.definition: The process of notifying relevant personnel when specific thresholds or anomalous conditions are detected by monitoring systems, indicating potential issues.

CONCEPT_BLOB_STORAGE.name: Blob Storage
CONCEPT_BLOB_STORAGE.definition: Binary Large Object storage, a method of storing unstructured data objects (like images, videos, documents) in the cloud, often providing high scalability and durability.

CONCEPT_OBJECT_STORAGE.name: Object Storage
CONCEPT_OBJECT_STORAGE.definition: A data storage architecture that manages data as objects, offering a highly scalable and cost-effective solution for unstructured data, often synonymous with blob storage.

CONCEPT_DISTRIBUTED_FILE_SYSTEMS.name: Distributed File Systems
CONCEPT_DISTRIBUTED_FILE_SYSTEMS.definition: File systems that are designed to be distributed across multiple network servers, allowing for high availability, scalability, and shared access to files, often involving chunking and replication.

CONCEPT_GOOGLE_FILE_SYSTEM.name: Google File System (GFS)
CONCEPT_GOOGLE_FILE_SYSTEM.definition: A proprietary distributed file system developed by Google to provide scalable and reliable storage for large data-intensive applications, using chunking and a single metadata master.

CONCEPT_HDFS.name: HDFS (Hadoop Distributed File System)
CONCEPT_HDFS.definition: Hadoop Distributed File System, a distributed file system designed to run on commodity hardware, providing high-throughput access to application data, commonly used in big data ecosystems.

CONCEPT_URL_SHORTENER_DESIGN.name: URL Shortener Design Case Study
CONCEPT_URL_SHORTENER_DESIGN.definition: Design considerations for a system that takes a long URL and generates a short, unique URL, often involving hashing, base62 encoding, and database choices.

CONCEPT_RATE_LIMITER_DESIGN_CASE_STUDY.name: Rate Limiter Design Case Study
CONCEPT_RATE_LIMITER_DESIGN_CASE_STUDY.definition: Designing a system to control and limit the rate of requests from users or services, often using token bucket, leaky bucket, or window-based algorithms.

CONCEPT_NEWS_FEED_DESIGN.name: News Feed Design Case Study (Twitter)
CONCEPT_NEWS_FEED_DESIGN.definition: Designing a system like Twitter or Facebook's news feed, involving strategies for feed generation (fan-out push vs pull), data storage, and caching.

CONCEPT_CHAT_SYSTEM_DESIGN.name: Chat System Design Case Study (WhatsApp)
CONCEPT_CHAT_SYSTEM_DESIGN.definition: Designing a real-time messaging system like WhatsApp, covering message delivery guarantees, read receipts, group chat fan-out, and scalability.

CONCEPT_INSTAGRAM_DESIGN.name: Instagram Design Case Study
CONCEPT_INSTAGRAM_DESIGN.definition: Designing a photo-sharing social media platform, including image storage, feed generation, CDN usage, and user interaction features.

CONCEPT_VIDEO_STREAMING_DESIGN.name: Video Streaming Design Case Study (YouTube/Netflix)
CONCEPT_VIDEO_STREAMING_DESIGN.definition: Designing a video streaming service like YouTube or Netflix, focusing on video encoding pipelines, adaptive bitrate streaming, and CDN edge caching.

CONCEPT_RIDE_SHARING_DESIGN.name: Ride-sharing Design Case Study (Uber)
CONCEPT_RIDE_SHARING_DESIGN.definition: Designing a ride-sharing application like Uber, which involves geospatial indexing (e.g., quad-trees, geohashing), matching engines, and real-time location updates.

CONCEPT_CLOUD_STORAGE_SYNC_DESIGN.name: Cloud Storage Sync Design Case Study (Dropbox/Google Drive)
CONCEPT_CLOUD_STORAGE_SYNC_DESIGN.definition: Designing a cloud storage and synchronization service like Dropbox or Google Drive, covering file chunking, sync mechanisms, deduplication, and metadata management.

CONCEPT_WEB_CRAWLER_DESIGN.name: Web Crawler Design Case Study
CONCEPT_WEB_CRAWLER_DESIGN.definition: Designing a system to systematically browse and index the World Wide Web, considering BFS crawling, deduplication using Bloom filters, and politeness/rate limits.

CONCEPT_NOTIFICATION_SYSTEM_DESIGN.name: Notification System Design Case Study
CONCEPT_NOTIFICATION_SYSTEM_DESIGN.definition: Designing a system for sending various types of notifications (push, SMS, email), involving fan-out via queues, integration with providers, retries, and deduplication.

CONCEPT_TICKET_BOOKING_SYSTEM_DESIGN.name: Ticket Booking System Design Case Study
CONCEPT_TICKET_BOOKING_SYSTEM_DESIGN.definition: Designing a system for booking tickets, addressing critical issues like seat locking, concurrency control, and preventing double-booking in a distributed environment.

CONCEPT_ECOMMERCE_PAYMENT_SYSTEM_DESIGN.name: E-commerce Checkout / Payment System Design Case Study
CONCEPT_ECOMMERCE_PAYMENT_SYSTEM_DESIGN.definition: Designing an e-commerce checkout and payment system, emphasizing idempotency keys, distributed transactions, and handling long-running workflows with patterns like Saga.
